metadata.title: At 13x earnings, is Qualcomm the most overlooked AI chip stock?

content.text:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Investing.com — Wall Street's artificial intelligence rally has concentrated overwhelmingly on cloud data center silicon, leaving multi-billion-dollar hyperscaler trades heavily crowded. While architectural peers like Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) trade at more than 200 times earnings, Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) has been left behind at $165.41—changing hands at just 12.98 times trailing earnings following an extended period of smartphone cycle skepticism.
Yet the center of gravity in artificial intelligence is beginning to broaden. As hyperscalers contend with ballooning power consumption and data center bottlenecks, compute workloads are shifting toward on-device processing across laptops, smartphones, and connected automotive cockpits. Qualcomm provides both the physical silicon and the foundational patent architecture powering that transition.
That disconnect between steady licensing cash flow and a depressed cyclical multiple is what InvestingPro's ProPicks AI models look for. The system maintains Qualcomm across both the Tech Titans and Beat the S&P 500 strategies. In Tech Titans' active November portfolio, Qualcomm is paired with a focused group of high-margin technology leaders—including a specialized semiconductor foundry manufacturer, an enterprise collaboration software platform, and an essential cloud edge delivery network.
Edge processing allows machine learning models to run directly on hardware rather than renting capacity from distant cloud servers. Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite processors have established a critical footprint across next-generation AI personal computers, while its automotive segment is integrating identical compute capabilities into modern vehicle cockpits. Automotive revenue reached a record $1.6 billion in fiscal Q3 2026, up 61% year-over-year, lifting its total design-win pipeline beyond $45 billion.
Management has raised its target for the automotive division's fiscal 2026 exit run-rate to an annualized $7 billion to $8 billion. Concurrently, Qualcomm is establishing a presence in physical infrastructure through an agreement under which Amazon could acquire up to $60 billion of its AI processors over a 10-year horizon.
Anchoring that expansion is Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL), which collects royalties on virtually every cellular device sold worldwide regardless of component supplier. QTL generated an elite 69% earnings before taxes (EBT) margin in fiscal Q3 2026, delivering reliable cash flow that insulates the balance sheet during cyclical device slowdowns.
Near-term handset demand remains the primary headwind. Handset chip revenues contracted 26% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026, while Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) continues its multi-year transition toward proprietary modem components.
A high-margin business priced for permanent contraction
Valuation multiples illustrate the extent of market skepticism. At 12.98 times trailing earnings, Qualcomm is priced as though its cash generation is in structural decline. Yet consensus analyst projections compiled on InvestingPro project a brief 3.6% dip in fiscal 2027 EPS to $9.91 before rebounding to $12.68 in fiscal 2028.
InvestingPro's Fair Value models—which aggregate multiple discounted cash flow and relative multiple frameworks—benchmark Qualcomm at $187.68 per share, representing a 13.5% discount from current trading levels. The platform's Financial Health suite rates the company "Good," supported by $11.1 billion in operational cash flow generated in fiscal 2026. That cash generation funds a well-covered 2.1% dividend yield backed by 24 consecutive years of annual payout increases.
Wall Street consensus targets reflect similar valuation headroom, centering on $197.03 with estimates ranging between $100 and $400. While seven downward earnings revisions against three upward adjustments over the past 90 days show analysts remain cautious regarding smartphone volumes, the current valuation provides a substantial buffer against further guidance cuts.
Investors can evaluate full automotive backlog timelines, QTL licensing margin durability, and Snapdragon PC market adoption inside the Qualcomm Pro Research Report.
Qualcomm's long-term thesis does not depend on an immediate smartphone boom. If on-device inference continues to migrate into laptops, vehicles, and consumer electronics, Qualcomm's silicon and patent portfolio are already embedded across the ecosystem, even as the market values the stock like a legacy handset vendor.
Capturing these fundamental dislocations before market sentiment normalizes is the objective of ProPicks AI. Rather than chasing crowded high-multiple momentum, the Tech Titans strategy systematically allocates capital toward proven cash generators across semiconductor manufacturing, developer software, and enterprise networking.
